context.title: Jehu's Furious Ride
context.summary: A young prophet anoints Jehu king and charges him to destroy Ahab's house. Jehu kills Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah, and Jezebel is thrown from a window and eaten by dogs.
context.background: The Tel Dan Stele, an Aramean inscription found in northern Israel in the 1990s, claims its author killed the king of Israel and a king of the 'house of David.' Most scholars credit it to Hazael and link it to these events; it is the earliest known mention of David's dynasty outside the Bible.

customs.note: Jezebel lined her eyes with dark cosmetic powder and dressed her hair, meeting Jehu like a queen.
Laying cloaks under a new king was an act of homage.

watchFor: Joram's body lands on Naboth's field, fulfilling Elijah's word (vv. 25–26).
Jezebel's taunt compares Jehu to Zimri, a seven-day usurper (v. 31).

people.name: Elisha
people.summary: God his salvation, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, who became the attendant and disciple of Elijah (1 Kings 19:16-19). His name first occurs in the command given to Elijah to anoint him as his successor (1 Kings 19:16).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: King of Israel, the son of Jehoshaphat (2 Kings 9:2), and grandson of Nimshi. The story of his exaltation to the throne is deeply interesting.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

people.name: Ahab
people.summary: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel, who exercised a very evil influence over him.

people.name: Jezebel
people.summary: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind.

people.name: Jeroboam
people.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

people.name: Baasha
people.summary: Bravery, the third king of the separate kingdom of Israel, and founder of its second dynasty (1 Kings 15; 16; 2 Chr. 16:1-6). He was the son of Ahijah of the tribe of Issachar.

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

people.name: Hazael
people.summary: Whom God beholds, an officer of Ben-hadad II., king of Syria, who ultimately came to the throne, according to the word of the Lord to Elijah (1 Kings 19:15), after he had put the king to death (2 Kings 8:15).

people.name: Joram
people.summary: The son of Ahab and Jezebel, and successor to his brother Ahaziah on the throne of Israel. He reigned twelve years, B.C. 896-884 (2 Kings 1:17; 3:1).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.summary: The son of Joram, or Jehoram, and sixth king of Judah. Called Jehoahaz (2 Chr. 21:17; 25:23), and Azariah (2 Chr. 22:6). Guided by his idolatrous mother Athaliah, his reign was disastrous (2 Kings 8:24-29; 9:29).

people.name: Naboth
people.summary: Fruits, “the Jezreelite,” was the owner of a portion of ground on the eastern slope of the hill of Jezreel (2 Kings 9:25, 26). This small “plat of ground” seems to have been all he possessed.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Zimri
people.summary: Murdered Elah at Tirzah, and succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He reigned only seven days, for Omri, whom the army elected as king, laid siege to Tirzah, whereupon Zimri set fire to the palace and perished amid its ruins (11-20).

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

places.name: Ramoth-gilead
places.summary: Heights of Gilead, a city of refuge on the east of Jordan; called “Ramoth in Gilead” (Deut. 4:43; Josh. 20:8; 21:38). Here Ahab, who joined Jehoshaphat in an endeavour to rescue it from the hands of the king of Syria, was mortally wounded (1 Kings 22:1-36).

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town of Issachar (Josh. 19:18), where the kings of Israel often resided (1 Kings 18:45; 21:1; 2 Kings 9:30). Here Elijah met Ahab, Jehu, and Bidkar; and here Jehu executed his dreadful commission against the house of Ahab (2 Kings 9:14-37; 10:1-11).

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Gur
places.summary: A whelp, a place near Ibleam where Jehu’s servants overtook and mortally wounded king Ahaziah (2 Kings 9:27); an ascent from the plain of Jezreel.

places.name: Ibleam
places.summary: People-waster, a city assigned to Manasseh (Josh. 17:11), from which the Israelites, however, could not expel the Canaanites (Judg. 1:27). It is also called Bileam (1 Chr. 6:70).

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:21), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh (Judg. 1:27), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon (1 Kings 4:12; 9:15).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Reign of Jehu
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 9:2–10:36. People: Jehu. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 28 years.
